game.name: Blazing Beaks
game.short_description: Roguelite - where too much greediness can be fatal. A colorful world with armed birds blazing their way through piles of mutants, monsters and creepy creatures. Lots of mysteries to unravel, secrets to discover and levels to explore.

commentary.label: Tier list Part 1 (2023)
commentary.summary: Blazing Beaks is a top-down shooter roguelike where you play as birds with guns. Its hook is that enemies drop cursed items with only downsides, and you choose how many to carry to the shop, where they can be swapped for beneficial items. He loves the concept, art and sound design, but finds the actual game suffers from design and balance problems. He never feels powerful, dies often on first visits to new areas, and puts it in D while respecting it.
praise: Cursed-item-for-shop-exchange mechanic is a really cool concept and gimmick
Sound design is amazing and very cute
Some cursed items have unique, interesting negative effects
He respects the idea and says it is fine if others like it
criticism: Never feels powerful or satisfying when progressing through a run
Shop items are random and often not game-changing, sometimes all useless
Only two to three health, so new areas usually kill you until you learn enemy attacks
Learning patterns per new area forces restarts
Runs feel not very impactful between characters or weapons
Curse design got more effort than the rewards, which were underwhelming
unique_points: Enemies drop downside-only cursed items that you trade in at the shop for useful ones
The push-your-luck question of how many curses to grab before the shop
Design effort seemed concentrated on the curses rather than the rewards
commentary.quote: not a huge fan I'll put it as a d
design_criteria: Power progression: run should feel increasingly powerful and satisfying
Risk vs reward: curse collection traded for shop rewards
Item quality and randomness: rewards need to be impactful, not useless
Difficulty and health: very low health punishes unfamiliar areas
Run variety: characters and weapons should make runs feel different
Art and sound design: charming and cute, strongly praised

community.one_liner: A pixel-art twin-stick roguelite where armed birds fight through randomized rooms, hauling back cursed artifacts that carry debuffs, with solo, local co-op and local PvP tournament modes.
community.consensus_summary: Blazing Beaks is well liked but a niche, under-the-radar title: Steam sits at Very Positive (about 83.5% of roughly 2,600 reviews), and critics on Switch landed around 80-81. Reviewers and players praise the charm, art, music, tight controls and the risk/reward artifact loop, and it shines in local co-op. The main complaints are a lack of meaningful meta-progression, heavy RNG (weapons and artifacts), uneven balance, and a sense that runs get samey; many negative reviews come from players expecting Nuclear Throne or Enter the Gungeon depth. Several recent Steam reviewers describe the game as effectively left dead on PC, though a mod/Workshop scene exists and a dev Discord community is still described as alive. Steam owner estimates are low (under 20k by SteamSpy; about 13 concurrent players), and revenue estimates are modest (around $265k gross / $78k net per a Boxleiter-style calculator).
best_things: Charming, clean pixel-art style with distinct, readable characters and enemies
Risk/reward artifact system: treasures carry debuffs (for example cannot shoot while moving) and you must survive to a shop to cash them in for a big power spike
Music repeatedly called out as some of the best in the genre
Tight, responsive twin-stick controls and a satisfying 'nuclear throne-like' feel
Fun local co-op for two players in story mode plus a four-player local tournament mode with five sub-modes
Eight birds with distinct stats and quirks (chicken accuracy that drops when moving, platypus extra loot, penguin cloning)
High replay value through randomized rooms, items and secrets, and a looping endgame that can go on indefinitely; Steam Workshop character mods
Good value and varied enemy behaviors; bosses need specific strategies
worst_things: Little or no sense of meta-progression: unlocks mostly dilute the item pool and nothing builds toward a long-term goal
Heavy RNG: weapons are scarce and random, artifacts cannot be planned around, and some runs reach the first boss with no artifacts
Balance is uneven: some guns and artifacts are strictly worse, many items are plain HP ups, and a couple of birds (Blue Bird, Chicken) outclass others (Duck, Seagull)
Some enemies and rooms feel unfair (for example unclear charge-up attacks, hitboxes and momentum-based movement) while bosses can feel easier than regular rooms
UI problems: some menus cannot be used with the mouse, gamepad aiming is called imprecise, and there are remote play/focus glitches and a launch failure report
Levels are small and repetitive with one boss type per biome; runs feel samey after several hours
Often viewed as a weaker clone of Nuclear Throne or Enter the Gungeon
No online multiplayer; it is local only, and PC is Windows only
improvements: Add real meta-progression or goals (for example a relic checklist or a good ending for collecting everything)
Make artifact drops more consistent, and rebalance weapons, artifacts and the weaker characters
Add online play or better remote-play support
Fix UI: full mouse support in menus and better gamepad aiming
Give more control over builds or weapon upgrading rather than pure RNG
Improve boss difficulty curve and late-game power scaling, and add more boss and level variety per biome
unique_things: Cursed-artifact economy: you carry debuffs and must reach a shop to exchange them for permanent buffs, so greed can kill you
Anthropomorphic bird cast with per-character positive and negative traits
Campaign plus a four-player local arena tournament in the same package
Looping endgame that can go on indefinitely
tedious_or_disliked: Runs feel samey and repetitive after a few hours because of small levels and predictable enemies
Forced RNG reliance: a good run can feel one in a million because of unfair environments
Weak upgrade system, for example tiny percent bonuses per coin, and filler items like plain HP ups
Steep learning curve and unforgiving difficulty; more frustrating than fun for some
Solo play is seen by some as much less fun than co-op
Frustration and rage moments: even fans say it can make you rage out, and players note the game depends on overcoming frustration
divisive_points: Difficulty: fans say it is fair and skill-based and you die from mistakes, detractors call it unforgiving and luck-driven
No meta-progression: a purist 'true roguelike' feature for some, a dealbreaker for others
Comparison to Nuclear Throne and Gungeon: some call it a great alternative, others call it worse in every way
Solo versus co-op: best with friends, but solo experience is judged weaker by some
community.reception_notes: Critic scores (Metacritic 80 from 9 reviews on Switch, OpenCritic 81 from 11 reviews, mostly Nintendo-focused outlets) come from the console release; Metacritic user score was 7.4 from 56 ratings on the page fetched (a search snippet showed 7.9 from 37, so it may have shifted). Steam lists a May 10, 2019 release (the game had earlier 2017 roots; the Steam date was not verified as early access). Early Steam community threads show Applava promising boss and artifact rebalancing and a weapons review, but recent Steam reviewers (2026) describe the game as dead/left without updates while still praising a dev Discord. It has Steam Workshop mod support, Steam trading cards, and is also on Switch, PS4 and Epic. Price is $14.99 and it is often on sale. Note that Metacritic and OpenCritic pages could not be confirmed from Steam, which lists no Metacritic score.
